title: Literal evaluation and rewind
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with $k$ work tapes, and let $w$ and $u$ be Boolean words. Fix a saved configuration of $M$ on input $w$, bits $a,c,b\in\{0,1\}$, an index $v\in\mathbb{N}$ with $v<|u|$, and Boolean words $\mathrm{pre}$ and $\mathrm{rest}$ such that $w$ is the concatenation of $\mathrm{pre}$, the word obtained by doubling each bit of the encoding $1^{v+1}0b$ of the literal $(v,b)$, and $\mathrm{rest}$. Starting from the evaluator's canonical configuration at input position $|\mathrm{pre}|$, with semantic phase $1$, formula bit $a$, clause bit $c$, skip flag cleared, and certificate head at $0$, after $3v+8$ steps it is in the canonical configuration at input position $|\mathrm{pre}|+2(v+3)$, with phase $1$, formula bit $a$, clause bit $c\vee(u_v=b)$, skip flag cleared, and certificate head at $0$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
A saved configuration of $M$ on input $w$
$w$ is the concatenation of $\mathrm{pre}$, the doubled encoding of $(v,b)$, and $\mathrm{rest}$
replaced:
Suppose the evaluator's input contains, at the current position, the doubling of a
serialized literal $(v, b)$ with $v < |u|$ for the certificate $u$. Starting in the
clause phase with clause bit $c$, exactly $3v + 8$ steps process the literal: the
input advances by $2(v + 3)$, the certificate head walks to position $v$, the
polarity is compared with the $v$-th certificate bit, the clause bit becomes
$c \vee (u_v = b)$, and the certificate head returns to $0$.
